concepts.name: Agile Manifesto values
concepts.summary: Recall the four Agile values and explain that they favour individuals, working software, collaboration and responding to change while still valuing the items on the right.

concepts.name: Twelve Agile principles
concepts.summary: Explain key principles such as early and continuous delivery, welcoming changing requirements and sustainable pace.

concepts.name: Iterative incremental delivery
concepts.summary: Describe how delivering work in small time-boxed increments allows feedback and adaptation, in contrast to a single big-bang delivery.

concepts.name: Scrum roles
concepts.summary: Name the three Scrum accountabilities and state what each is responsible for.

concepts.name: Time-boxing
concepts.summary: Understand that Scrum events and sprints have fixed maximum durations and why fixed length supports rhythm and focus.

concepts.name: Scrum events
concepts.summary: List the Sprint, Sprint Planning, Daily Scrum, Sprint Review and Sprint Retrospective and state the purpose of each.

concepts.name: Scrum artifacts
concepts.summary: Explain the Product Backlog, Sprint Backlog and Increment and how each relates to a commitment.

misconceptions.text: Agile means no planning and no documentation.
The Scrum Master is the project manager who assigns tasks to the team.
Scrum is a methodology that prescribes every practice in detail.

concepts.name: Writing user stories
aliases: As a, I want, so that
concepts.summary: Write user stories in the role-goal-benefit format that describe value from a user's perspective.

concepts.name: Acceptance criteria
concepts.summary: Write testable criteria that define when a story meets expectations.

concepts.name: Product backlog ordering
concepts.summary: Order backlog items by value, risk and dependencies so the most important work is at the top.

concepts.name: Story point estimation
concepts.summary: Estimate items relatively in story points using techniques such as planning poker.

concepts.name: Sprint planning steps
concepts.summary: Run planning by agreeing a sprint goal, selecting backlog items and breaking them into tasks in the sprint backlog.

concepts.name: Daily Scrum conduct
concepts.summary: Use the 15-minute Daily Scrum to inspect progress toward the sprint goal and adapt the plan for the next day.

concepts.name: Kanban board basics
concepts.summary: Use a board with columns for workflow states to visualise work and its status.

misconceptions.text: Story points measure the number of hours a task will take.
The Daily Scrum is a status report to the Scrum Master or manager.
A user story is a detailed specification written once and then frozen.

concepts.name: Velocity-based forecasting
concepts.summary: Use average completed points per sprint to forecast how much work and how many sprints a backlog needs.

concepts.name: Burndown and burnup charts
concepts.summary: Read burndown and burnup charts to diagnose scope change, slippage and risk to the sprint goal.

concepts.name: Definition of Done
concepts.summary: Analyse how a shared quality standard makes the Increment transparent and prevents hidden unfinished work.

concepts.name: Backlog refinement
concepts.summary: Break down, clarify and estimate upcoming items so they are ready for planning, applying splitting patterns such as INVEST.

concepts.name: Effective retrospectives
concepts.summary: Analyse sprint problems, find root causes and turn them into a small number of actionable improvements.

concepts.name: Sprint review feedback
concepts.summary: Demonstrate the Increment to stakeholders and turn feedback into backlog changes.

concepts.name: WIP limits and flow
concepts.summary: Analyse how limiting work in progress improves flow and exposes bottlenecks on a Kanban board.

concepts.name: Scrum Master servant leadership
concepts.summary: Apply coaching, facilitation and impediment removal to help the team self-manage.

misconceptions.text: A higher velocity means a team is more productive and teams can be compared by velocity.
Partially finished stories count toward velocity or the sprint review.
Retrospectives are for blaming individuals and do not need follow-up actions.

concepts.name: Scaling Agile approaches
concepts.summary: Analyse coordination needs across multiple teams and compare scaling approaches and their trade-offs.

concepts.name: Value-driven prioritisation
concepts.summary: Evaluate prioritisation techniques and select one fitting the context of value, cost of delay and uncertainty.

concepts.name: Agile metrics evaluation
concepts.summary: Judge which metrics such as cycle time, throughput and escaped defects give useful signals and which invite gaming.

concepts.name: Scrumban hybrid
concepts.summary: Assess when to combine Scrum's cadence with Kanban's flow practices and adapt the process accordingly.

concepts.name: Team dynamics and conflict
concepts.summary: Diagnose issues such as low trust, dominant members or weak ownership and select interventions.

concepts.name: Release and roadmap planning
concepts.summary: Evaluate release plans and outcome-based roadmaps that balance commitment and uncertainty.

concepts.name: Technical practices for agility
concepts.summary: Analyse how engineering practices enable frequent, sustainable delivery of a Done increment.

misconceptions.text: Scaling frameworks can be adopted wholesale to make a large organisation agile.
Scrumban or Kanban means abandoning planning and improvement events.
Agile metrics should be used as targets to evaluate individual performance.

concepts.name: Critiquing Agile dogma
concepts.summary: Evaluate Agile practices critically against evidence, identifying ritual without purpose and when plan-driven methods suit better.

concepts.name: Outcome-oriented product governance
concepts.summary: Create governance and funding models that steer by outcomes and validated learning rather than output and fixed scope.

concepts.name: Coaching teams and leaders
concepts.summary: Develop coaching approaches that grow team maturity and shift leaders from directing to enabling.

concepts.name: Empirical process control theory
concepts.summary: Evaluate how empiricism underpins Scrum and use it to judge whether adaptations preserve its feedback loops.

concepts.name: Designing tailored Agile systems
concepts.summary: Create a working approach for an organisation by composing practices while preserving core Agile principles.

concepts.name: Agile transformation strategy
concepts.summary: Design a staged change plan addressing structure, incentives, leadership behaviour and culture.

concepts.name: Agile in regulated contexts
concepts.summary: Judge how to meet audit, safety and contractual demands while keeping iterative delivery.

misconceptions.text: A transformation is complete once all teams follow Scrum events correctly.
Agile cannot be used in regulated or fixed-contract environments.
Experts should enforce the framework exactly as written regardless of context.
